article_title: Enhancing clinical reasoning in medical students: A novel pedagogical approach integrating a virtual patient platform with mind mapping.
citation: Huang L, Zhu Y, Zhang Y, Zhu W, Fang L, Chen L. Enhancing clinical reasoning in medical students: A novel pedagogical approach integrating a virtual patient platform with mind mapping. Medicine 2026;105:4(e47273). https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000047273
title: DxR-Clinician virtual patient platform for interactive simulated diagnosis and treatment
description: The DxR-Clinician system "converts all real-case data into digital resources and presents them in the form of virtual patients through online simulation scenarios." Students "conduct interactive diagnosis and treatment through computer networks, such as by asking questions, conducting physical examinations, selecting clinical examinations and diagnostic tests, and carrying out treatment." Each operation ends with a summary of results (Evaluations 1 to 7), instructors review step-by-step performance through a management interface, and students receive an overall assessment comparing their responses to the instructor's expected diagnosis.
requirements: Two clinical instructors with experience in teaching using the DxR-Clinician system and excellent teaching capabilities were selected to run the model.
constraints: The platform was implemented during the 2-week community internship stage of general practice with a case library of 20 clinical case studies, mainly involving the respiratory, digestive, and nervous systems.
examples: The reform group completed 3 of the 20 cases in training sessions, with an "acute cough" case using an "asthma" case within the clinical resonance training program.
